'''Ryan Joseph Tibshirani''' (born December 15, 1985) is a professor and chair of the Department of Statistics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=berkeley-chair>{{cite web |title=Tibshirani Named Chair |url=https://statistics.berkeley.edu/about/news/tibshirani-named-chair |website=UC Berkeley Statistics |date=June 18, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref> His work spans high-dimensional statistics, nonparametric estimation, distribution-free inference, convex optimization, and epidemic tracking and forecasting.<ref name=imstat>{{cite web |title=Ryan Tibshirani wins the prestigious 2023 COPSS Presidents' Award |url=https://imstat.org/2023/08/31/copss-presidents-award-ryan-tibshirani/ |website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |date=August 31, 2023 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref name=amazon>{{cite web |title=Ryan Tibshirani, Berkeley professor and Amazon Scholar, wins COPSS Presidents' Award |url=https://www.amazon.science/news-and-features/ryan-tibshirani-berkley-amazon-scholar-committee-of-presidents-of-statistical-societies-presidents-award |website=Amazon Science |date=September 2023 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref name=berkeley-profile>{{cite web |title=Ryan Tibshirani |url=https://statistics.berkeley.edu/people/ryan-tibshirani |website=UC Berkeley Statistics |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Tibshirani was born on December 15, 1985 in  Toronto, Canada.
He earned a B.S. in Mathematics from [[Stanford University]] in 2007 and a Ph.D. in Statistics from Stanford in 2011; his dissertation, ''The Solution Path of the Generalized Lasso'', was advised by Jonathan Taylor.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ryan Tibshirani |url=https://statistics.stanford.edu/people/ryan-tibshirani |website=Stanford Department of Statistics |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD thesis |title=The Solution Path of the Generalized Lasso |author=Tibshirani, Ryan J. |publisher=Stanford University |year=2011 |url=https://stacks.stanford.edu/file/druid%3Adx901bd1560/thesis-augmented.pdf}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 2011 to 2022, Tibshirani was a faculty member in the Department of Statistics and Department of Machine Learning at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] (CMU).<ref>{{cite web |title=Ryan Tibshirani (archived CMU profile) |url=https://www.stat.cmu.edu/~ryantibs/ |website=Carnegie Mellon University |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref> He joined UC Berkeley in 2022 and became department chair effective July 1, 2025.<ref name=berkeley-chair/>

Tibshirani is a principal investigator with the Delphi Research Group, which develops epidemic tracking and forecasting systems in collaboration with the [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] (CDC), as well as other partners.<ref>{{cite web |title=Delphi Group Awarded $17.5 million from CDC |url=https://statistics.berkeley.edu/about/news/delphi-group-awarded-175-million-cdc |website=UC Berkeley Statistics |date=November 15, 2023 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Unveil interactive COVID-19 tracking at county level |url=https://medicalxpress.com/news/2020-04-unveil-interactive-covid-county-level.html |website=Medical Xpress |date=April 17, 2020 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Facebook and Google share data to forecast coronavirus |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2020/04/09/998924/facebook-and-google-share-data-to-forecast-coronavirus/ |website=MIT Technology Review |date=April 9, 2020 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rosenfeld |first1=Roni |last2=Tibshirani |first2=Ryan J. |title=Epidemic tracking and forecasting: Lessons learned from a tumultuous year |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=118 |issue=26 |year=2021 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2111456118 |pmid=34903658 |pmc=8713795 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 2023, he became Editor-in-Chief of ''Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning'', taking over from founding Editor [[Michael I. Jordan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning — Editorial Board |url=https://www.emerald.com/ftmal/pages/editorial-board |website=Emerald Publishers |access-date=June 14, 2026}}</ref> In 2024, he became founding co-Editor-in-Chief of ''Foundations and Trends in Statistics'' with [[Rina Foygel Barber]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Foundations and Trends in Statistics — Editorial Board |url=https://www.emerald.com/ftstat/pages/editorial-board |website=Emerald Publishers |access-date=June 14, 2026}} </ref>

== Research ==
Tibshirani’s research focuses on methodology and theory for high-dimensional and nonparametric problems, often connecting statistical inference with convex optimization.<ref name=imstat/><ref name=amazon/> He has made important contributions to regularization and sparsity methods, including the lasso, generalized lasso, and trend filtering, developing both theoretical guarantees and efficient algorithms.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tibshirani |first1=Ryan J. |last2=Taylor |first2=Jonathan |title=The solution path of the generalized lasso |journal=Annals of Statistics |volume=39 |issue=3 |year=2011 |pages=1335–1371 |doi=10.1214/11-AOS878 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-statistics/volume-39/issue-3/The-solution-path-of-the-generalized-lasso/10.1214/11-AOS878.full|arxiv=1005.1971 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Tibshirani |first=Ryan J. |title=Adaptive piecewise polynomial estimation via trend filtering |journal=Annals of Statistics |volume=42 |issue=1 |year=2014 |pages=285–323 |doi=10.1214/13-AOS1189 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-statistics/volume-42/issue-1/Adaptive-piecewise-polynomial-estimation-via-trend-filtering/10.1214/13-AOS1189.full|arxiv=1304.2986 }}</ref> He has also contributed to selective inference, to distribution-free predictive inference (conformal prediction), and to epidemic modeling and forecasting.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lockhart |first1=Richard |last2=Taylor |first2=Jonathan |last3=Tibshirani |first3=Ryan J. |last4=Tibshirani |first4=Robert |title=The solution path of the generalized lasso |journal=Annals of Statistics |volume=42 |issue=2 |year=2014 |pages=413–468 |doi=10.1214/11-AOS878 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-statistics/volume-42/issue-2/A-significance-test-for-the-lasso/10.1214/13-AOS1175.full|arxiv=1005.1971 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lei |first1=Jing |last2=G'Sell |first2=Max |last3=Rinaldo |first3=Alessandro |last4=Tibshirani |first4=Ryan J. |last5=Wasserman |first5=Larry |title=Distribution-free predictive inference for regression |journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association |volume=113 |issue=523 |year=2018 |pages=1094-1111 |doi=10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Ryan Tibshirani is the son of statistician [[Robert Tibshirani]], with older brother Charlie Tibshirani, and younger sister Julie Tibshirani who is a co-creator generalized random forests.<ref>{{cite web |title=Generalized Random Forest|url=https://grf-labs.github.io/grf/ |access-date=August 9, 2025}}</ref> He is married to Jessica Tibshirani (née Issler) and they have two children.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Ryan Tibshirani - Other |url=https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~ryantibs/other.html |website=UC Berkeley |access-date=August 9, 2025}}</ref>
